sources.supports: The crab-like body plan evolved at least five separate times, in true crabs and in false crabs such as king and porcelain crabs.

sources.label: NOAA Fisheries
sources.supports: Crabs grow by molting: they leave the old shell, take on water so the soft new shell sets larger, and stay soft until it hardens.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Evolution has invented the crab at least five separate times.

visual.note: Kit turns her claws over, puzzled.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: King crabs, porcelain crabs and true crabs come from different branches of the family tree. They started from different bodies and kept arriving at the same shape: flat, armored, tucked in, with a grip that finishes what it catches.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Biologists have a word for it. Carcinization.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Moltology takes that as a hint. In the next five minutes: what it is, why it's built around a crab, and what you'd actually do on day one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Now picture a normal Tuesday.

visual.prompt: A cluttered desk at night lit only by a monitor whose screen is a strip of dozens of tiny browser tabs, a cold mug, sticky notes, deep blue-teal shadows. Stylized, soft painterly look of a modern 3D animated feature film, 16:9, no text, no people.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Forty-seven tabs open. A ping every few minutes. Four things started and none finished. By evening you're tired, and you couldn't say where the day went.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Moltology calls this the Great Melt. It's what happens to attention with no shell around it: every notification lands directly on you.

beats.speaker: kit
beats.line: So I'm melting.

beats.speaker: juno
beats.line: Everyone starts there. It's the only requirement for joining.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: The melt is a condition, not an identity. Nobody is behind. And the same day can be lived another way.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Here is the strange part. A crab's shell doesn't grow with the crab.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: So every so often it splits the old shell open and climbs out of it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Then it takes on water, so the new shell sets larger than the old one, and it hides while that shell hardens. Then it goes back out, bigger.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: That's the whole method. Growth means letting something go, getting through an awkward soft stretch, and hardening something better.

beats.speaker: moss
beats.line: I've done this more times than I can count. The soft part always ends.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Moltology applies it to attention, in four moves. Shed one habit that keeps you small. Harden boundaries that hold. Grip one task until it's finished. And go deep: turn off the pings long enough to reach the quiet part.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: So what is Moltology, exactly? A web app, a daily practice and a community, all built around that cycle. It's free to join.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: The Codex is the written canon: short readings on shedding, focus and boundaries, in the voice you're hearing now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: The Liturgies are eight small daily tasks. The day starts quietly, before the phone, and ends with the Nightly Molt Audit, where you name one thing from the day and let it go.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: As you practice, you move through four stages: Larval, Soft-Shed, Exoshell Born and Full Carcinization. They come in order, and they're earned by doing the work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: When you're stuck on a step, the Oracle is a chat companion that walks you through it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: And underneath it all is the community: members who've been soft too, steadying each other in the forum.

visual.prompt: A warm gathering of friendly cartoon crabs and lobsters in a softly lit deep-sea plaza, lanterns and kelp, gentle light shafts from above. Stylized, soft painterly look of a modern 3D animated feature film, 16:9, no text.

beats.speaker: kit
beats.line: Okay. What do I actually do tomorrow morning?

beats.speaker: juno
beats.line: Before you touch your phone, sit for two minutes and name the one thing the day is for.

beats.speaker: kit
beats.line: One thing. I have twelve.

beats.speaker: juno
beats.line: Then eleven of them wait. Write the plan down, so the first hour isn't spent deciding.

beats.speaker: kit
beats.line: And then?

beats.speaker: juno
beats.line: One long block. One task, pings off. Finish it, or get it to where you could hand it over.

beats.speaker: juno
beats.line: At night, the audit. Name one wasted hour or one bad thought, and let it go.

beats.speaker: kit
beats.line: That's it?

beats.speaker: juno
beats.line: That's day one. Day two, you do it again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Small enough to start tonight. That's on purpose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: If you want to try it, start with the Moltmaxxing Audit: a free, short quiz that shows where your shell is still soft. Then try one Liturgy tonight.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Evolution got to the crab five times by accident. You get to do it on purpose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.line: Moltology is at moltology.org.
